abstract.t: This document defines the PRP Self-Certifying Identifier Reference (SCIR), a compact typed reference for an IDENTITY, ALIAS, MULTICAST, or GROUPCAST. A SCIR contains a reference class, a closed initial suite value, and a suite-sized cryptographic commitment to class-specific immutable certifying material. It is an identifier rather than a machine address, locator, session, credential, or authorization.

The document defines the canonical representation, the five initial suites, IDENTITY and ALIAS formation, class separation, rejection behavior, and deterministic formation vectors. URI, QR Code, DNS, and protocol-specific proof carriers are specified separately.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Applications need stable typed references independently of the machine, address, route, transport connection, or representative currently serving them. The PRP Self-Certifying Identifier Reference (SCIR) provides one envelope for IDENTITY, ALIAS, MULTICAST, and GROUPCAST identifiers.

“Self-certifying” means that a verifier can recompute the identifier from disclosed immutable certifying material. For IDENTITY, that material is a canonical public key and a consuming protocol can additionally verify key possession. For ALIAS it is canonical text. MULTICAST and GROUPCAST commit to immutable canonical genesis material. A SCIR is not a certificate, does not sign itself, and does not establish mutable authority, membership, control, administration, civil identity, or application compatibility.

The relationship-centric PRP architectural model is described informatively in . This document is self-contained for SCIR syntax, formation and validation and does not make conformance depend on an architectural publication revision.

section.name: Canonical Binary Representation
section.t: The canonical SCIR consists of:

The low two bits of reference_header contain the reference class. The admitted complete values are 0x00 IDENTITY, 0x01 ALIAS, 0x02 MULTICAST, and 0x03 GROUPCAST. Bits 7 through 2 are reserved and zero. A parser MUST reject every other value and MUST NOT mask reserved bits or coerce one class to another.

reference_suite is a complete 16-bit suite value. It is not a format version or a session-protection suite. L is fixed by the recognized suite. There is no identifier-length field and no inner format-version field. An unassigned suite, incorrect total length, truncation, or trailing octet is invalid in a field defined to contain exactly one SCIR.

section.name: Closed Initial Reference-Suite Set
section.t: This document assigns exactly the following five values. Public-key sizes are in octets. Strong-ID hashes SHA-256 and SHA-384 are defined by . The Ed25519 public-key encoding is defined by , ML-DSA public-key encodings by , and BLAKE3 by .

For IDENTITY, suites 0x0001 and 0x0002 use the exact 32-octet Ed25519 public-key encoding. Suite 0x0003 uses the exact ML-DSA-65 public-key encoding, and suite 0x0004 uses the exact ML-DSA-87 public-key encoding. Suite 0x0005 encodes its canonical public key as Ed25519[32] || ML-DSA-87[2592]. Both components are committed.

For the other classes, the public-key column does not apply; the suite's hash and exact identifier length do apply. Every class therefore has a 35-octet SCIR under suites 0x0001, 0x0002, 0x0003, and 0x0005, and a 51-octet SCIR under suite 0x0004.

The numeric values and names preserve existing PRP identity-suite assignments. This document projects them only onto SCIR formation: canonical public-key encoding, commitment hash, and Strong-ID length. It neither defines nor changes a possession-proof operation or proof length. A consuming protocol that uses the same value MUST define its complete operation, inputs, component order, purpose, context, transcript, freshness, role binding, canonical verification, and rejection behavior. Proof semantics MUST NOT be inferred from a suite mnemonic.

All other 16-bit values are unassigned in this version and MUST be rejected. There is no private-use range, implementation-defined allocation, or negotiation by observed length. Existing values MUST NOT be reassigned or given new semantics.

section.name: IDENTITY Strong-ID and SCIR Formation
section.t: Let S be the identity-suite value encoded as an unsigned 16-bit big-endian integer, and let PK be the exact canonical public-key encoding selected by S. The Strong ID is:
HASH_S and its output length are fixed by the suite. No NUL octet, length prefix, textual suite spelling, reference header, or carrier field participates in this preimage. The SCIR is:

Suites remain distinct even when their hash output lengths match, because S participates in both the preimage and the SCIR. Public keys MUST be canonical before hashing. A parser or producer MUST NOT normalize, decompress, reorder, or reinterpret public-key bytes.

For BLAKE3 suites, HASH_S is the unkeyed hash mode specified by . The Strong ID is the first 32 output octets beginning at XOF output offset zero. keyed_hash, derive_key, a nonzero seek offset, or another output selection MUST NOT be used.

For an operational IDENTITY SCIR, every public-key component MUST successfully pass the decoding and public-key validity checks required by its referenced algorithm. The verifier MUST canonically re-encode the decoded key and compare it octet-for-octet with PK before hashing. Suite 0x0005 components are checked independently and retained in their specified order. An invalid or noncanonical encoding MUST be rejected, not normalized.

section.name: IDENTITY Validation and Possession
section.t: Given an expected SCIR and a presented public key, a verifier MUST:

ol.li: parse an exact SCIR and require reference_header 0x00;
resolve an assigned identity suite and its exact lengths;
validate the suite's canonical public-key encoding;
recompute the Strong ID as specified in ;
compare the complete recomputed SCIR with the expected SCIR; and
verify the possession evidence defined by the consuming protocol, using the validated key and that protocol's exact operation and domain.

section.t: Strong-ID equality without a valid possession proof is insufficient for authenticated interaction. A valid possession proof does not authenticate a DNS name, application parameter, alias membership, representative authorization, or civil identity unless another applicable protocol binds and validates that statement.

When a service is represented, the principal SCIR remains the expected identity. The representative proves its own identity and supplies separately authenticated authorization. A representative key or identity MUST NOT replace the principal Strong ID in the expected SCIR.

section.name: ALIAS Formation
section.t: An ALIAS is a global, application-independent rendezvous identifier derived from canonical text. Different applications obtain the same ALIAS when they intentionally use the same text and reference suite. No application profile, creator, member, role, authority, or nonce is part of ALIAS certifying material.

alias_text MUST be a nonempty Unicode scalar-value sequence, normalized to NFC as specified by and then encoded as UTF-8 as specified by . The resulting T MUST contain 1 through 1024 octets and MUST NOT contain U+0000 or a C0 or C1 control character. Case, punctuation, and whitespace are otherwise significant.
section.sourcecode: alias_identifier = HASH_S( ASCII("PRP-SCIR-ALIAS-v1") || 0x01 || S:u16be || len(T):u32be || T ) alias_scir = 0x01 || S:u16be || alias_identifier
section.t: len(T) is the number of UTF-8 octets. HASH_S uses the suite hash and exact output length. A verifier presented with alias text MUST apply the same canonicalization, recompute the complete ALIAS SCIR, and compare every octet. This proves only the committed text; membership, selection, role, and application compatibility require separate authenticated evidence.

section.name: MULTICAST and GROUPCAST Formation Boundary
section.t: MULTICAST and GROUPCAST are SCIR classes whose identifiers commit to immutable canonical genesis material. Mutable controllers, administrators, participants, incorporated groups, sessions, locators, and application state are not identifier fields. Their exact genesis encoding and authority evidence are specified by the managed-reference profile. Until that profile is admitted, an implementation MUST NOT invent local certifying material and claim an interoperable MULTICAST or GROUPCAST SCIR.

section.name: Equality, Canonicalization, and Replacement
section.t: Two SCIRs are equal only when their complete octet strings are equal. Equality includes the header, suite, and identifier. Implementations MUST NOT compare only digest bytes or infer a suite from length.

A change of suite or certifying material produces a different SCIR. Identity key rotation is reference replacement rather than an in-place update. Continuity, migration, revocation, and authorization across two SCIRs require a separate authenticated statement.
The binary SCIR has exactly one encoding. A human interface MAY abbreviate it for diagnostics, but an abbreviation is not a SCIR and MUST NOT be accepted as interoperable input.

section.name: Carrier Boundary
section.t: This document defines the exact binary SCIR only. URI, QR Code, DNS, and protocol-message carriers are separate specifications. A carrier MUST NOT redefine SCIR formation or infer its length from available input. An enclosing carrier that permits application parameters after a SCIR MUST determine the SCIR boundary from the assigned suite and treat the remaining octets as carrier data, not as a SCIR extension.
Carrier proximity does not authenticate application parameters. A carrier specification must define its own canonical encoding, size bounds, parsing, and security properties.

section.name: Extensibility
section.t: A future normative revision can assign another reference suite only by defining its numeric value, commitment hash, identifier length, applicable canonical material, security properties, and deterministic vectors. A consuming protocol independently specifies any possession profile it associates with IDENTITY. Unknown and unassigned suites fail closed.

All four headers are SCIR classes but do not inherit IDENTITY formation or possession semantics merely because they share an envelope. A future incompatible SCIR grammar requires an explicitly recognizable successor; decoders MUST NOT guess from length or reserved bits.

ul.li: The security strength of a SCIR is bounded by its suite, hash, and class-specific certifying material.
A syntactically valid or correctly formed SCIR does not authenticate its supplier.
Possession of identity keys, alias-text equality, or genesis validity does not itself grant application, membership, control, administration, or relationship authority.
Downgrade and cross-suite fallback are prohibited. Equal field lengths do not establish compatibility.
A verifier must bind possession evidence to the consuming protocol's exact purpose, transcript, roles, and freshness rules.
Private keys, session secrets, and private application data are never SCIR fields.
Parsers must validate suite and exact size before allocation and must fail closed on unassigned values, reserved bits, truncation, and trailing data in an exact-SCIR field.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: A stable SCIR permits correlation across publications, applications, carriers, and time. Applications should disclose a SCIR only where a stable reference is required and should not treat the absence of a civil name or network address as anonymity. Public DNS or QR disclosure makes the stable pseudonym observable. Replacement does not ensure unlinkability when the same public key, a migration statement, or the same application account exposes continuity. Suite choice can fingerprint implementation capability or policy. A SCIR has no embedded revocation or freshness, so a carrier or cache can retain an obsolete reference. User interfaces should distinguish verified identity information from untrusted labels and abbreviations.

Human-readable or low-entropy ALIAS text is enumerable by dictionary attack. Parties requiring an unguessable rendezvous value should share high-entropy alias text; adding an application identifier to the ALIAS would fragment the intended global rendezvous namespace and is not a privacy mechanism.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document has no IANA actions. The reference-suite namespace is closed to the five assignments in . This document neither creates an IANA registry nor delegates suite allocation to another registry. A future standards action can revise the closed set or create a registry without changing an existing assignment.

section.name: Required Rejection Cases
section.t: An exact-SCIR parser MUST reject each of the following:

ul.li: any header other than 0x00 through 0x03, including a nonzero reserved bit;
suite 0x0000 or any value other than 0x0001 through 0x0005;
one-octet-short, one-octet-long, truncated, or trailing input;
a 48-octet Strong ID under any suite other than 0x0004; and
a valid identifier presented with a different suite or class;
an empty or greater-than-1024-octet canonical ALIAS text; and
ALIAS text containing U+0000 or a C0 or C1 control character.
